lines.text: The one heading for the sign that says "To your disk".
That's the record. Every tile that goes into the tray is written there too, and saved on your disk: the transcript. Your prompt, every reply, every call and every result.

lines.text: Why keep two copies?

They do different jobs. The tray is what gets sent to the model. The record is what happened, kept so a session can be picked up again later. Claude Code keeps each session as a file under ~/.claude, and claude --resume opens one again. Codex keeps them under ~/.codex, and codex resume does the same.

lines.text: And when it gets there?
The press. A separate model call writes a summary of the session: the goal, what was decided, what's left to do. In the tray, that one orange block takes the place of the old turns.

lines.text: So the model forgets how the session went.
It keeps the gist and loses the detail. Say the summary notes that three runs out of twenty failed. The model no longer sees the output that said so.

lines.text: Does every agent have a press?

Each its own kind. Claude Code compacts by itself near the limit, or when you type /compact, and a PreCompact hook can save what you need first. In Codex, /compact asks for a summary from your side, and the server can also compact in the middle of a reply and hand back a sealed item. Copilot's summarizer watches the budget and can squeeze the old turns in the background, before the limit bites.
